main_text.p: Particip. ἡμένος, καὶ ἀνήμενος, καὶ ἐνησόμενος.
8. εἷμαι indutus sum: εἵμην, εἶσαι, (Poetice ἕασαι) εἶται & εἶσαι. Tertia pluralis εἶντ̃αι: Ionicè ἕαται.
Aor. 1. εἶσα, εἶσας, εἶσε, &c. Poet. ἕσα, ἕσας, ἕσσε, quod etiam est collocare.
Horist. 1. εἵμην, & rejecto incremento assumptoq; σ, ἔσμαι, unde ἀμφιέσμαι circumamictus sum.

4. εἵμλω, εἶσο, εἶτο & εἶσο. 3 pluralis εἶντο, ἕατο & εἵατο, induti vel collocati erant, vel sedebat, unde comp. παρείατο assidebant. Nam horist. 1. est pro praesenti primo, & quartum pro infecto secundo. Aliquando etiam in horistico quarto est ἑσμλω, ἕσο, (poet. ἕασο) ἕσο, indutus vel locatus erat.

page.notes: Greek forms are transcribed approximately; several accents and breathings in the Greek are uncertain. The final "Aorist." at lower right is treated as a catchword-like signature word.
